headline: VidTube Channel That Only Rates Different Types of Rain Reaches 2 Million Subscribers
subheadline: Creator @PluviophileReviews has categorized 847 distinct rain varieties
summary: A VidTube channel dedicated exclusively to reviewing precipitation has become a surprise phenomenon.
content:
A VidTube channel called "Rain Ratings" that does exactly what it says—rates different types of rain on a 10-point scale—has reached two million subscribers, making creator @PluviophileReviews one of the platform's most unlikely success stories.

"People think rain is just rain," explained the creator in a recent video reviewing a "misty drizzle with occasional heavier patches" (8.3/10). "Those people are wrong. There are 847 documented rain types and I will review them all."

The channel launched in 2022 with a simple premise: sit outside during precipitation and provide detailed commentary on the rain's qualities. Categories include droplet size, sound quality, "cozy factor," petrichor intensity, and "would I take a walk in this."

Recent top-rated rains include a "gentle autumn shower with golden hour lighting" (9.7/10), "post-thunderstorm mist" (9.4/10), and "that specific type of rain that somehow comes from a clear sky" (9.8/10 for mystery bonus).

Lowest rated was "cold horizontal rain that somehow gets under your umbrella" (2.1/10), with the creator noting "this rain is personally attacking me and I will not be rating it higher."

The channel has inspired a dedicated community on Threadit where fans debate rain rankings and share their own precipitation experiences. A recent controversy erupted over whether "freezing rain" qualifies as rain or belongs in a separate ice category.

"I've been watching rain my whole life," commented subscriber @DrizzleDisciple. "I never knew I was missing out on professional analysis. Now I can't experience precipitation without mentally rating it."

The creator has partnered with weather services to receive alerts for unusual rain events and has traveled to document regional variations. A recent video comparing "Seattle drizzle" to "UK drizzle" generated 847,000 views.

"My life's work is telling people about moisture falling from the sky," said @PluviophileReviews. "And honestly? It's exactly as fulfilling as it sounds."
author: Tom Hendricks, Media Correspondent
